role: Declares the native world core: struct chunk (Chunk with ExtendedBlockStorage flattened into per-cell id/meta/sky/blocklight arrays plus height maps and section bookkeeping) and struct world (the chunk map, load order, light update list, tile entity lists, dimension providers and probe hooks), and the world_* / chunk_* API implemented in world.c.

structs.name: chunk
structs.java: Chunk with its ExtendedBlockStorage sections flattened (block ids, metadata, sky and block light per cell), height maps, section mask, relight flags, tile entity map, inhabitedTime, biome array and the tick bookkeeping (tickRefCount per section, populated flags, queuedLightChecks)

structs.name: world
structs.java: World plus ChunkProviderServer: the loaded chunk map and loadedChunks order, lightUpdateBlockList, field_147482_g / field_147484_a / field_147481_N tile entity lists, the provider dimension (WorldProviderHell / WorldProviderEnd) and harness hooks mirroring netherite.oracle.Rows.onBlock / onAttempt

structs.name: chunk_sec
structs.java: ExtendedBlockStorage: blockLSBArray inline, blockMSBArray (ids_hi), and the metadata, sky light and block light NibbleArrays out of line (nib[k] self-relative offsets into the arena's nibble pool, or one of its sixteen constant arrays when every nibble is one value; lane/chunkmem)

gpu: line 58, struct world: chunks are individually heap-allocated and held through an open-addressing table of pointers (struct chunk **slot); a GPU mirror needs a fixed chunk pool indexed by slot, not a pointer graph
line 63, struct world: near[256] is a mutable direct-mapped pointer cache in front of the map
line 64, struct world: load_order is a growable heap array (lon/locap); iteration order is carried as data, which is GPU friendly, but its growth reallocates inside the tick

lines 73-91, struct world: te_list, te_added, te_reg and te_registry are growable arrays of pointers to individually allocated tile entities (a pointer graph, with allocation when a tile entity is created in the tick)
line 42, struct chunk: tes (struct te_store, chunkTileEntityMap) holds tile entity pointers per chunk

lines 105-141, struct world: function-pointer hooks (on_block, on_drop, provide, on_attempt, on_attempt_end, on_chunk) with void* contexts; the provide hook loads chunks from disk in the whole-server replay
lines 31-34, struct chunk: four CHUNK_CELLS arrays per chunk (ids is uint16), so per-chunk state is about 160 KiB whether or not sections exist

world_get_block and world_get_meta are static inline (lane/chunkspeed): a chunk in the map's near cache is read in place, anything else takes world_get_block_slow / world_get_meta_slow (world.c); struct world gains the light pass's chunk window (map_ver, lwin*, lbox*), a cache only
notes: Header only; the implementation is world.c. world_set_meta is declared twice (lines 182 and 226) with two slightly different comments, harmless in C. Both te_reg (line 78) and te_registry (line 90) are described as the per-world registry of every tile entity ever held; what distinguishes the two was not verified here. The test list is the tests that include or call world_* functions (grep), not a check that each covers every entry point. world.c references both te_reg and te_registry (6 hits each). Lane gpuphase (GPU audit L6): struct chunk and struct world carry wseq, a write sequence every block, metadata and light write and every insertion moves (chunk_touch, chunk_set_meta, world_note_write), which the phase digests read to hash the chunks a phase wrote. A band (struct chunk_sec) carries shared, the chunks holding it besides one: chunk_share makes a copy that shares the source's bands (the client's copy of a server chunk, a chunk packet in flight, play's render records), and a store of a different value into a shared band first makes it the chunk's own (chunk_sec_own), so each chunk reads what it would with bands of its own (lane/gpumem, L9). struct chunk_backend gains take and owed, struct world gains backend_ctx (lane/gpugen, genahead.h). lane/coldaudit: the overworld provider gen is built at its first use (world_gen, gen_made); light_list (World.lightUpdateBlockList) moved to env.h struct env_scratch.
